summary: A quieter weekend: Carney draws a line on autos in US trade talks, Stelco recalls 175 Hamilton steelworkers, and former Liberal ministers say Canada will miss its 2030 climate target.
body: Wrapping up the ASEAN summit in Manila, Prime Minister Mark Carney said trade talks with the US are progressing, but "this government will not settle for a deal with the United States that is not consistent with a viable Canadian auto sector."[^1] He also said Ottawa is "not satisfied in any way" with Stellantis's "partial approach" after it sold its Brampton plant to Roshel.[^1] Carney announced $540 million for a rainforest protection fund co-led by Brazil and Norway, drawn from Canada's existing climate-finance pledge, and has moved on to the Francophonie summit in Cambodia before APEC in China later this week.[^2]

In Hamilton, Stelco's US owner Cleveland-Cliffs will recall 175 laid-off steelworkers on Dec. 1 and repay their lost wages.[^3] Industry Minister Mélanie Joly had said the layoffs broke promises the company made when Ottawa approved its 2024 takeover, and had warned she could seek a court-ordered sale; the company denies breaking its commitments. The local union president said government pressure worked, but "we didn't need to get to this point."[^3]

At COP31, Environment Minister Julie Dabrusin said Canada is "absolutely committed" to its target of cutting emissions 40 to 45% below 2005 levels by 2030. Emissions were about 10% below 2005 in 2024, and the federal environment commissioner projects a 28% cut by 2030 after policies such as the consumer carbon price were dropped. Two former Liberal environment ministers, Catherine McKenna and Steven Guilbeault, called her claim untrue; her office calls the government's approach "pragmatic and durable."[^4]
For students: Ontario's bill to tighten OSAP at private career colleges is due to be tabled on Monday, Nov 16.[^5]
differences: Former ministers McKenna and Guilbeault say Canada has no chance of meeting its 2030 climate target; Dabrusin says Canada is a leader, pointing to methane cuts and climate finance.[^4] Joly says Cleveland-Cliffs broke its takeover commitments; the company denies it.[^3]
